# Registering for GST
**Last updated** 14 September 2026

## How GST registration works
You only need to register for GST once, even if you operate more than one business.

You only need to register for GST once, even if you operate more than one business.

## When you need to register
You must register for GST:

- if you earn income through the sharing economy or digital platforms (for example, food delivery services or other platform-based work). For more information, see [Sharing economy](https://www.ato.gov.au/tax-and-super-professionals/for-tax-professionals/prepare-and-lodge/tax-time/before-you-lodge/sharing-economy).

## If you don't register
You need to register within 21 days of your GST turnover exceeding the relevant threshold.

# Selling to Australia Without GST Registration? The ATO Already Knows
## Summary
- Non-resident merchants, platform operators and redeliverers must register for Australian GST once GST turnover from supplies connected with Australia reaches A$75,000, counting imported services, digital products and low value imported goods together. About 3,000 are registered and over 90% use simplified registration, which gives an ATO reference number but no GST credits and no tax invoices.

Nine years later, more than 3,000 non-resident businesses are registered.

## Frequently asked questions
Simplified registration is online, gives the business an ATO reference number rather than an ABN, and runs on quarterly returns.

The ATO can register it compulsorily and issue a default assessment based on its own calculation, with a 75% penalty on top (90% for repeat non-compliance) and general interest charge at 11.51% a year for October–December 2026.

# Registrations
## On this page
- [Registration requirements](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/income-deductions-and-concessions/sharing-economy-and-tax/ride-sourcing/registrations#ato-Registrationrequirements)
- [How to register](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/income-deductions-and-concessions/sharing-economy-and-tax/ride-sourcing/registrations#ato-Howtoregister)

## Registration requirements
The standard GST registration rule for GST turnover of $75,000 or more does **not** apply when it comes to ride-sourcing – you have to register for GST regardless of how much you earn.

## How to register
**If you already** **have an ABN but haven't registered for GST yet**, you have to register within 21 days from the time you start providing ride-sourcing services. You can register for GST online, by phone or through your registered agent.

web.description:
# How to Register for GST in Australia: When You Must and How to Do It
## When Is GST Registration Compulsory in Australia?
### What Happens If You Exceed $75,000 Temporarily?
The ATO requires you to register if you ‘could reasonably expect’ your turnover to remain above the threshold going forward.

## How GST Works for Different Business Types
### Ride-Share and Delivery Drivers
[Delivery drivers](https://www.hrblock.com.au/tax-academy/tax-deductions-delivery-riders) (Uber Eats, DoorDash, Menulog) are treated differently: they are only required to register once their total income from all sources reaches $75,000, because they provide courier services rather than taxi travel.
